title: GDD T-102 — SessionStateMachine: full session FSM with per-state timeouts (§2.1/§2.2)
description: Extend/wrap the existing RoundPhaseMachine (Barcade.Core — do NOT rewrite it; add states, per Annex D.1) into a SessionStateMachine covering the full GDD §2.1 graph: ATTRACT -> JOIN -> (BOARD_MOVE -> BOARD_RESOLVE -> MG_INTRO -> MG_PLAY -> MG_RESULT -> INTERMISSION)* -> FINAL_WAGER -> FINAL_MG -> GAME_OVER -> ATTRACT. Board states are part of the FSM now but pass through as stubs until BoardModel (Hito 4) is wired. FSM invariants from the GDD: no transition ever blocks on input (every state has a timeout, §2.2 budget table); MG_PLAY is the only state where gameplay input reaches the active microgame; state serializes per tick for deterministic replay (§13). JOIN: each player claims a color with a button press, needs >= 2 ready players, 30 s timeout; GAME_OVER returns to ATTRACT after 20 s. Read GDD §2 before coding.
acceptance_criteria: SessionStateMachine implements every state and transition of GDD 2.1 including JOIN color-claim (>=2 players, 30 s timeout), the round loop, FINAL_WAGER, FINAL_MG, and GAME_OVER (20 s timeout back to ATTRACT)
Every state has a timeout from the GDD 2.2 budget table and a session driven with zero input still reaches GAME_OVER (no state can be blocked by an absent player)
Only MG_PLAY forwards gameplay input to the active microgame; all other states accept only confirmation taps / minimal navigation
BOARD_MOVE and BOARD_RESOLVE exist as pass-through stubs (advance in <= 1 tick when no board model is wired) so Hito 4 slots in without changing the FSM shape
FSM state is a serializable POCO and the machine is deterministic: same (seed, input sequence) produces an identical state trace (replay test)
Existing RoundPhaseMachine consumers keep compiling and passing (extension, not rewrite)
Tests-first: failing fast-suite tests for the invariants above committed strictly before implementation; suite green after with no regression
